mutations.because: The pre-lane spelling, restored -- and it is restored by anyone who reads `applyRefusal` as "the refusal Save owes after committing", which is exactly what its name and its docstring said for D35's whole life. It survives almost everything: a LOADED brief is committed (`fromBrief` sets `appliedSnapshot`), so the reason is on screen in every existing motion test and in the first half of this lane's own capability test. The case it loses is the one a real operator reaches -- edit a loaded motion draft, press Validate -- where `applied` is false, Generate is disabled, and the status line goes back to saying `status.loaded` ("press Validate, then Generate"): a disabled verb beside a sentence telling the operator to press it, with the reason nowhere on the page. Disabling a control is only honest while the reason is shown (DESIGN.md's capability rule), so this mutation does not soften the fix, it makes it worse than the defect. Caught by the edited-draft test, which types one character before validating and asserts the sentence is the refusal and NOT `status.loaded`.

mutations.because: SG-D15 as it stood: freshness is the `state` reference and nothing else, which section 8.4 argued was EXACT. The argument is airtight about the document and silent about the second argument `validateState` is given, and that silence is the defect -- `existingIds` comes from the brief listing, which refetches on window focus, so the errors can move while `state` does not. Under the mutation every document-keyed test in the repo still passes, including all four of section 8.4's own, because not one of them changes the listing: the projection case, the refused-action case and the real-edit case are all decided before this line is reached. What it restores is a gate that reports "still validated" over a validation that has stopped holding -- the likely shape being an id that was unique when it was judged and is taken by the time Generate is pressed, so the operator is charged for a run the API then refuses. mutations.because: The consistent spelling, and the reason it is wrong is the whole subtlety of this half: the document is compared BY REFERENCE one line above, for very good reasons section 8.4 spends a page on, so comparing the ids the same way looks like the same decision applied twice. `existingIds` is `briefs.map(...)`, a new array on every render and a new one again after every refetch, so reference equality here answers "stale" always -- Generate would appear for the render of the Validate press and be gone on the next one, which no assertion made immediately after a click can see. The stale-gate test above passes under it, and so does every test that presses Validate and then Generate synchronously. That is the trade this lane was warned about: a gate that never goes stale because it never stays fresh. mutations.because: The copies dropped as waste -- `.sort()` mutates, so `[...a]` looks like defensive cloning someone added out of habit, and with the clones gone the sort has nothing to protect and goes too. Positional comparison of two lists with the same contents is right in every test that builds both lists itself, which is every test in this file. The listing is not positional, though: it is the set of ids that exist, and the API is free to return them in whatever order it stored or sorted them in. Under the mutation a refetch that returned the same briefs in a different order reads as a changed listing and takes the operator's validation away -- the constant-reset failure, arriving by a route the crude `a === b` mutation does not cover. Caught by the unit test's reorder assertion, which passes the same two ids swapped and requires the validation to stand.
command: a listing refetch that changed nothing leaves a good validation standing
